rule: Make interactive touch targets at least 24×24 CSS pixels; prefer 44×44 for comfort.
quote: Interactive targets must be at least 24x24 CSS pixels in size.
finding: Average adult fingertip covers roughly 10mm (about 40px on a typical phone display)

rule: Space adjacent touch targets at least 8 pixels apart to prevent accidental activation.
quote: Space targets apart. Even if each target is 24px, placing them 2px apart forces precision. Aim for at least 8px spacing between adjacent targets.

rule: Pad small icons to expand the interactive hit area beyond the visual element.
quote: Size the target, not just the icon. The interactive hit area should extend beyond the visual element. Padding is your tool.

rule: Include essential contact details in footers to build trust and let users reach the organization.
quote: Contact information in the footer serves as a quick reference point for users who may need to get in touch with your organization.

rule: Provide footer navigation links to important sections so users can explore without scrolling back up.
quote: A strategically organized footer increases user engagement by providing one more opportunity for visitors to take desired actions, such as signing up for a mailing list or viewing a product demo.

rule: Communicate your organization's purpose at a glance on the homepage.
quote: Don't make people guess — studies indicate that failing to communicate a site's purpose at a glance causes potential customers to abandon the site.

rule: Showcase examples of content offerings on the homepage to encourage exploration.
quote: homepages should showcase samples of the site's offerings. Doing so encourages further exploration and helps users quickly determine if the site contains what they're looking for.

rule: Organize footer links into 4–6 logical columns with clear headers grouping by user intent.
quote: Keep it organized. Use columns with clear headers to group related links. Limit yourself to 4–6 columns maximum.

rule: Keep tooltip text under 150 characters, aiming for 1–2 lines; use a popover for longer content.
quote: Keep it short. Aim for 1–2 lines, ideally under 150 characters. If you need more, consider a popover instead.

rule: Use a small arrow caret to visually connect the tooltip to its trigger element.
quote: Arrow indicator: Use a small triangular arrow (caret) pointing from the tooltip to the trigger element. This visually connects the tooltip to its context.

rule: Implement collision detection so tooltips automatically reposition to stay within the viewport.
quote: Viewport awareness: Implement collision detection so the tooltip automatically repositions when it would otherwise extend beyond the screen.

rule: Use proportional columns to ensure consistent page layout across different screen sizes and devices.
quote: Responsive grids are built using proportions, which helps elements line up properly when users view the site on different screens.

rule: Add gutters between columns and rows to separate elements visually and establish relationships between page sections.
quote: Gutters are the space between columns or rows in your design. They're a crucial part of responsive grids, providing visual separation between different elements while giving your page a cohesive look and feel.

rule: Use margins to establish visual hierarchy and prevent elements from overlapping unnecessarily on the page.
quote: Margins help establish visual hierarchy and ensure that elements don't overlap unnecessarily. By adding white space between elements, margins make it easier for users to differentiate between different sections on the page without being overwhelmed by too much information at once.

rule: Define breakpoints at specific screen sizes where layout changes to optimize content display across devices.
quote: Breakpoints allow designers to optimise their design for different screen sizes. In essence, breakpoints refer to the specific points where a website layout changes.

rule: Use cards with rounded corners and subtle shadows to make content appear as distinct blocks that pop from the page.
quote: Cards should have rounded corners and short shadow. Rounded corners make card look like a content block, while shadows gives the impression of depth.

rule: Keep cards within a layout at constant width but allow variable height to accommodate different content types.
quote: Cards from the same layout should have a constant width, but can have variable height.

rule: Implement card gestures consistently within a collection and prevent overlapping swipe actions like cards and carousels.
quote: Card gestures should be consistently implemented within a card collection. Limit swipe gestures within a view so that they don't overlap with one another.

rule: Use card-based layouts to display content in digestible chunks that scale responsively across desktop and mobile devices.
quote: Cards offer content in more digestible chunks. They are good choose for responsive design since cards act as content containers that easily scale up or down.

rule: Make modals visually distinct from background with strong border or shadow so users perceive the context shift.
quote: Modals must be visually distinct from the background to help users understand the shift in context.

rule: Ensure text contrast ratios are at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text in modal dialogs.
quote: Text vs background contrast ratio ≥ 4.5:1 (normal text) or ≥ 3:1 (large text)
finding: 4.5:1 contrast ratio for normal text; 3:1 for large text

rule: Trap keyboard focus inside modal so users cannot tab into background content while the modal is open.
quote: A user should never be able to 'tab out' of the modal into the background content while it's open.

rule: Return focus to the trigger button when modal closes so screen reader users do not lose navigation position.
quote: When the modal closes, the focus must return to the button that opened it.

rule: Close modals when users press Escape key to provide an expected and keyboard-friendly dismissal method.
quote: Escape: Closes the modal and returns focus to the trigger button.

rule: Make close button and action buttons at least 24px by 24px (44px on mobile) to accommodate limited dexterity.
quote: Ensure the 'Close' button and any action buttons are at least 24px x 24px (preferably 44px on mobile) to accommodate users with limited dexterity.

rule: Use aria-describedby to provide context for why the modal appeared, improving understanding for all users.
quote: aria-describedby='ID': Points to the main description text of the modal. This provides immediate context for why the modal appeared.

rule: Group filter categories and truncate display after a predetermined number, adding links to reveal remaining options.
quote: Filter categories group the filters—for example, price, brand, size, category, etcetera—and help users get an immediate sense of how much data will be left after refining the search results by a specific attribute.

rule: Express hierarchical relationships between filter options in the interface controls themselves to enforce correct usage.
quote: When an explicit relationship exists between the filtering options in a set, it may be preferable to expose that relationship within the filtering controls.

rule: Limit contact forms to three fields maximum to increase completion rates.
quote: those who cut the form field number from four to three get a 50% increase in those users who complete forms
finding: 50% increase in form completion when reducing from 4 to 3 fields

rule: Place form field labels above or to the right of input fields, never elsewhere.
quote: Place form field labels above or on the right of the input field

rule: Use single-column layouts for forms; never use multiple columns.
quote: Never use multiple columns in the form

rule: Enable browser autofill to reduce abandonment and increase form submission rates.
quote: when Chrome disabled the feature, the rate for form submissions was down 25%
finding: 25% decrease in form submissions when autofill was disabled

rule: Highlight form errors in a distinct color like yellow or orange for immediate visibility.
quote: Those fields with errors can be either highlighted in a different color, like yellow or orange

rule: Use switches only for settings that apply instantaneously without requiring a submit button.
quote: Switches should never require users to press a button to apply the settings because a switch is a toggle button

rule: Use background color contrast with the navigation menu to prevent banner blindness.
quote: Use a background color that contrasts with your navigation menu but complements your brand palette

rule: Avoid complex gradients and background images in announcement bars to preserve text readability on mobile.
quote: avoid complex gradients or background images in the bar; they reduce text readability, especially on mobile devices

rule: Avoid rapid blinking or scrolling ticker-tape animation; use subtle slide-in or fade effects instead.
quote: Don't: Use rapid blinking or scrolling ticker tape text. It feels dated and cheapens the brand perception

rule: Use geo-targeting to display location-specific announcement bar messages to different regions.
quote: Use geo-targeting to display Free US Shipping only to IP addresses in the United States

rule: Reserve CSS space for announcement bars before page loads to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift penalties.
quote: reserve space in the CSS before the content loads

rule: When using countdown timers, show realistic end states; do not reset timers immediately to maintain trust.
quote: If you use a countdown timer, ensure what happens when it hits zero is realistic. If the timer resets immediately, customers will notice

rule: Apply the same animation or visual effect consistently for the same action throughout the interface.
quote: The same animation or visual effect should be used for the same action throughout the interface

rule: Use subtle motion in micro-interactions to enhance feedback without competing with primary content.
quote: Deference refers to fluid motion and a crisp, visually appealing interface that facilitates understanding and interaction with the content while never competing with it

rule: Respond promptly to user input with immediate visual feedback in micro-interactions.
quote: Effective micro-interactions should respond promptly to user input, providing immediate feedback

rule: Use generous negative space in interfaces to evoke luxury and sophistication.
quote: Copious amounts of negative space lend connotations of luxury and sophistication

rule: Employ macro and micro whitespace rhythms to frame understanding and emphasize important interface elements.
quote: The rhythms of your macro- and micro-whitespace can help frame understanding, lead the reader down the page, and emphasize important elements

rule: Reduce rather than add to designs; solve problems by doing less, not more.
quote: when a design isn't working, the instinct can often be to add more—more lines, more color, more design—when in reality, the answer is so often, do less

rule: Center the hero section composition with headline in middle and graphic below for stability and trust.
quote: the hero section is centered: a big, bold headline in the middle of the screen, with a supporting graphical element placed right below. This looks stable, feels trustworthy, and it just works.

rule: Avoid flashy interactions; focus on clean design with solid typography and clear layout instead.
quote: Most pages avoid flashy interactions. They focus on clean design: solid typography, clear layout, and enough breathing room.

rule: Use centered layout with max-width container; it is simple, readable, and quick to build.
quote: Almost all pages use a centered layout with a max-width container. It's simple, readable, and quick to build.

rule: Avoid salesy language and use clever, simple messaging on developer tool landing pages.
quote: No salesy BS. Clever and simple wins.

rule: Avoid difficult words with three or more syllables on landing pages.
quote: Difficult words (three or more syllables) show the strongest negative link to conversion, a correlation of -24.3%.
finding: difficult words show -24.3% correlation with conversion

rule: Keep copy short; reduce total word count and reading time to improve conversion.
quote: Reading time (-19.4%) and total word count (-18.6%) also pull conversion down.
finding: reading time and word count show -19.4% and -18.6% correlation with conversion

rule: Users spend 57% of viewing time above the fold; place key content there.
quote: Users spend about 57% of their page-viewing time above the fold.
finding: 57% of viewing time is above the fold; top half of screen gets 65%+ of above-fold viewing

rule: Delay popup display by 6 to 10 seconds for best conversion over instant display.
quote: A 6 to 10 second delay converts best at 2.4%, while popups shown instantly convert at 1.9%.

rule: Show popups on mobile devices; desktop-only popups convert at 1.4% versus 2.2% on mobile.
quote: Desktop-only popups convert at just 1.4%, against 2.2% for popups shown on mobile.

rule: Target popups to specific pages rather than sitewide for better conversion.
quote: Popups targeted to specific pages convert at 2.4%, versus 2.0% for sitewide popups.

rule: Position decoy pricing tier between basic and premium but closer to premium in value.
quote: The decoy should sit between your basic and target plans in price, but closer to your target plan in value delivery. I typically position decoys at 70-85% of the target plan's price while delivering only 40-60% of the value.
finding: adding decoy plan at $79 increased professional ($89) plan selection from 27% to 61%; revenue per customer +$47

rule: Anchor pricing page by showing premium plan first to increase revenue per visitor.
quote: At a Fortune 500 energy company, we tested anchoring on the pricing page by showing the premium plan first instead of the basic plan. Revenue per visitor increased by 18%.
finding: showing premium plan first: 18% revenue increase per visitor; support tickets dropped 12%

rule: Display customer testimonials on landing pages to increase conversions.
quote: one study found that displaying customer testimonials on a landing page increased conversions by 34%.

rule: Use real customer testimonials and reviews rather than fake or fabricated ones.
quote: Keep it real: use real customer testimonials, reviews, and endorsements, rather than fake or fabricated ones.

rule: Excessive options impair choice-making ability and induce decision paralysis per Hick's law.
quote: Hick's law dictates that too many options will impair the user's ability to make a choice. It induces decision paralysis.

rule: Rank information by importance and use card sorting to organize complex architectures.
quote: A more complex information architecture can be useful if you rank pieces of information from more to least important. Exercises such as card sorting can be very useful for this.

rule: Avoid comparison tables when more than six products with 15+ features overwhelm users.
quote: If you have too many features or options (e.g., more than 6 products with 15+ features each), comparison tables can overwhelm users and cause decision fatigue.

rule: Maintain consistency, scannability, and simple layout for successful comparison tables.
quote: Consistency in content, scannability, and a simple layout are some of the most important qualities of successful comparison tables.

rule: Expect only 1% of visitors to interact with carousels, with 84% of clicks on the first slide.
quote: Only 1% of visitors:inside clicked on a slide at all and of those, 84% of clicks were on the first one. The remaining slides were barely noticed or ignored.
finding: 1% of visitors clicked carousel slides; 84% of those clicks were on slide one

rule: Avoid carousels on mobile; provide visual cues or explicit prompts for swipe interactions.
quote: Without clear visual cues or interaction prompts ("Swipe me"), the carousel simply goes unnoticed or is misunderstood.

rule: Carousels are treated as banner blindness; visual presence does not guarantee interaction.
quote: Carousels are noticed, but often ignored as advertising or irrelevant content. The visual presence therefore does not automatically lead to interaction or understanding.

rule: Ensure tooltips adapt responsively on mobile; they must adjust dynamically based on screen size and layout shifts.
quote: What works beautifully on a desktop could break on a mobile screen. Your tooltips should adjust dynamically based on screen size and layout shifts, ensuring a seamless experience across devices.

rule: Make the team page mobile-responsive; images and text must scale appropriately on smaller screens.
quote: The page must be optimized for smaller screens. This includes using responsive design techniques to ensure that images and text scale appropriately and that the layout remains user-friendly on all devices.

rule: Keep animations fast and prioritize user-perceived performance over technical benchmarks.
quote: Animations should be fast and nimble, never keeping the user waiting longer than is necessary. The aim is to prioritize user-perceived performance over technical benchmarks.

rule: Use negative space as an essential element of design composition, not merely as blank area.
quote: White space should not be considered merely "blank" space — it is an important element of design which enables the objects in it to exist at all; the balance between positive (or non-white) and the use of negative spaces are key to aesthetic composition.

rule: Set OK and Cancel button width to 68 pixels per Apple Human Interface Guidelines.
quote: The standard width for OK and Cancel buttons is 68 pixels
finding: Apple HIG specifies 68px width for OK and Cancel buttons on OS X

rule: Use a 12-column grid because it divides evenly into 2, 3, 4, and 6 columns for maximum layout flexibility.
quote: The 12-column grid is the most popular because 12 divides evenly into 2, 3, 4, and 6 columns.

rule: Adopt an 8-point spacing system using multiples of 8 px to maintain consistent vertical and horizontal rhythm.
quote: An 8-point spacing system (multiples of 8 px) keeps vertical and horizontal rhythm consistent.

rule: Embed grid tokens in a shared design system so all team members use identical spatial rules.
quote: Embedding grid tokens in a shared design system ensures every team member — and AI tools — use the same spatial rules.

rule: Remove every unnecessary form field to reduce abandonment; each field is an opportunity for users to make mistakes.
quote: Every field you add to a form is an opportunity for users to make mistakes or abandon the process.

rule: Use consistent dropdown structure with labels, trigger elements, menu containers, and selectable options to help users transfer knowledge.
quote: This consistency allows users to transfer their knowledge across different applications, reducing the learning curve.

rule: Return autocomplete results from the first keystroke to provide maximum responsiveness and user control.
quote: Make sure results are returned from the first keystroke for maximum responsiveness and user control.

rule: Include six to eight query suggestions in autocomplete menus to avoid overwhelming users with too many options.
quote: Include 6 to 8 query suggestions.

rule: Use inverted highlighting in autocomplete results, bolding untyped text to focus attention on what remains to be read.
quote: Prefer "inverted" highlighting. This places in bold the pieces that weren't typed, focusing user attention on what remains to be read.

rule: Make the search box full-width with a placeholder that tells users what to do, so it visually stands out on all devices.
quote: The search box should visually stand out, be full-width and include a placeholder that tells users what to do.

rule: Position search within natural thumb reach on mobile, avoiding top-center placement that requires stretching; center-bottom is ideal.
quote: Put it where people can see it. The Uniqlo and Mad Kicks sites do an excellent job of placing it centrally at the bottom of the screen, within close reach of the thumb.

rule: Place the search box on every page at the top right or center of the screen where users expect to find it.
quote: The search box should be available on every page of your website. Put it in a place users expect to see it. Research supports a search field that's integrated with your website's navigation, generally placed at the top right or center of the screen.

rule: Ensure autocomplete hit areas are appropriately sized to prevent small targets that lead to mistakes or frustration.
quote: Make sure you avoid small hit areas which can lead to mistakes or frustration. An appropriately sized hit area ensures that users can easily select the suggestion they want.

rule: Keep autocomplete suggestion lists to around ten items on desktop and eight on mobile to prevent analysis paralysis.
quote: When suggestions exceed around 10 items on desktop (and around eight on mobile), users either ignore suggestions or spend too much time reading through them.

rule: Make column headers clickable to allow users to sort and reorder data instantly by their chosen criteria.
quote: Users click a column header and reorder instantly. They compare numbers, dates, or names side by side.

rule: Set minimum button size to 42 pixels (9x9 mm) for accessibility and comfortable button size around 50 pixels (10x10 mm).
quote: Minimum button size should be 42 px (9×9 mm) for accessibility. Comfortable button size is around 50 px (10×10 mm), matching the fingertip area.

rule: Follow platform standards: Apple 44x44 points, Google 48x48 dp, or Microsoft 34x34 px plus spacing for touch-friendly buttons.
quote: Apple (44×44 pt), Google (48×48 dp), Microsoft (34×34 px + spacing) set size rules.

rule: Space buttons 12-48 pixels apart to prevent accidental taps and reduce user errors from too-close targets.
quote: Spacing of 12-48 px between buttons prevents accidental taps and errors.

rule: Use one primary button per screen to guide users toward the key task.
quote: each screen should have only one primary button

rule: Make primary action buttons filled with solid background color and high contrast from surrounding elements.
quote: They need solid background color, high contrast with surrounding elements, and clear labels that describe the action

rule: Position destructive buttons away from frequently used actions with enough padding to prevent accidental triggers.
quote: They should be placed away from frequently used actions and include enough padding to prevent accidental triggers

rule: Keep segmented controls between 2 and 5 options; more options become hard to read and tap.
quote: Keep the number of segments between 2-5 — more options become hard to read and tap accurately

rule: Use short, descriptive text labels in segmented controls that fit without truncation.
quote: Text labels should be short and descriptive and fit without truncation

rule: Prefer native HTML <dialog> with showModal() for true modal behavior; use existing primitives only if they provide focus, inertness, containment, Escape, and focus restoration.
quote: Prefer the native HTML <dialog> with showModal() for a true modal. It provides the modal behaviors required

rule: Give dialogs an accessible name using a visible heading with aria-labelledby; avoid aria-label unless necessary.
quote: Give the dialog an accessible name. Prefer a visible heading referenced with aria-labelledby

rule: Move focus to the first useful control for short forms, a static heading with tabindex="-1" for long content, or the least destructive action for irreversible decisions.
quote: Choose based on content: the first useful control for a short form, a static heading or introductory element with tabindex="-1" for long/structured content, or the least destructive action for an irreversible decision

rule: Support Escape key to close modals; ensure only the topmost dialog closes when modals can stack.
quote: Support Escape to close a modal, unless the product explicitly requires a different, documented behavior. Ensure only the topmost dialog closes when dialogs can stack

rule: Provide a clearly named visible close or cancel control; do not make backdrop-click the only dismissal mechanism.
quote: Provide a clearly named visible close/cancel control. Do not make backdrop-click the only dismissal mechanism

rule: Restore focus to the opener when the modal closes; if the opener was removed, choose the next logical workflow target.
quote: On close, restore focus to the opener when it still exists. If it was removed, choose the next logical workflow target and test that path

rule: Make dialog content scrollable without trapping the close control; preserve focus indicators and avoid clipping essential actions at narrow widths.
quote: Make the modal usable at narrow viewport widths: allow the dialog content to scroll without trapping the close control, preserve visible focus indicators, and avoid clipping essential actions

rule: Do not close a dialog on accidental outside click when it would discard entered data or interrupt a critical task.
quote: Do not close a dialog on an accidental outside click when it would discard entered data or interrupt a critical task without warning

rule: Avoid automatically showing a modal when a user lands on a page unless genuinely critical for security or data loss prevention.
quote: Arriving on a page is not considered user input. Avoid automatically showing a modal when a user lands on a page

rule: Use role="dialog" or native <dialog> element; add aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby or aria-label for accessibility.
quote: Use role="dialog" or the native <dialog> element. Add aria-modal="true" so screen readers know the background is blocked. Use aria-labelledby or aria-label to provide the modal's name

rule: For general dialogs, focus the first interactive element; for destructive actions, focus the least destructive option like Cancel.
quote: For general dialogs, focus the first interactive element. For destructive actions, focus the least destructive option (e.g., the Cancel button)

rule: Provide at least three ways to exit a modal: backdrop click, Escape key, and a footer button; include a close button if no Cancel button exists.
quote: Provide users with at least three ways to exit the modal: Clicking outside the modal (backdrop click). Pressing the Escape key. Using a footer button (e.g., Cancel or Close)

rule: Use specific button labels like "Delete File" instead of generic options; place primary action on the right, Cancel on the left in left-to-right languages.
quote: Be specific: Use labels like "Delete File" instead of generic options like "OK". Place the primary action on the right and the Cancel action on the left

rule: Maintain at least 40dp distance from left and right edges and 24dp from top and bottom; ensure content is 24dp from dialog edge.
quote: Maintain a distance of at least 40dp from the left and right edges of the screen, and 24dp from the top and bottom. Ensure the dialog's content is 24dp from the dialog edge

rule: On mobile, expand large modals to full width and use 75% screen width for small/medium modals; keep headers and footers fixed while allowing body to scroll.
quote: Large modals: Expand to full width on mobile devices. Small/medium modals: Use 75% of the screen width on mobile. Keep headers and footers fixed while allowing only the body content to scroll

rule: Avoid nested modals; use sequential modals, sidebars, drawers, tabs, or inline editing instead.
quote: Nested modals create a poor user experience (UX) for several reasons: Users may lose their place within the workflow. Cognitive overload increases with multiple layers

rule: Avoid vague error messages; use specific, helpful text like "Your session ended—please log in again" instead of "Error!".
quote: Vague error messages (e.g., "Error!" vs. "Your session ended—please log in again")

rule: Limit modal buttons to a maximum of three, including Cancel, to avoid overloading users.
quote: Overloading modals with too many buttons (stick to three maximum, including Cancel)

rule: When a dialog closes, return focus to the triggering element; if it no longer exists, move focus to a logical alternative to prevent keyboard users from losing their place.
quote: When a dialog closes and focus returns to the top of the page instead of the triggering element, keyboard users lose their place entirely

rule: Avoid nesting modals; if a secondary confirmation is needed, replace the current modal's content rather than layering a new dialog on top.
quote: Opening a modal from within a modal creates layered focus traps that are extremely difficult to manage correctly. Avoid nesting modals

rule: On mobile, lean toward higher contrast levels because screens are used in varying lighting conditions like direct sunlight or dim rooms.
quote: Mobile screens are frequently used outdoors or in varying lighting conditions, making contrast even more critical. Always lean toward higher contrast levels on mobile apps

rule: Allow text to resize up to 200% without triggering horizontal scrolling to ensure accessibility for users with vision impairments.
quote: Allowing text resizing up to 200% without horizontal scrolling
